newsitem.title: GERMANY: Father of Belgian child victim may enter politics. [CORRECTED 22:41 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Father of Belgian child victim may enter politics. [CORRECTED 22:41 GMT]

text.p: The father of a girl abused and murdered in Belgium's child sex scandal said in an interview on Sunday he will form a new political party to fight the government if new laws are not passed (corrects to make clear that Marc Dutroux has not been convicted of girl's murder).
"For months the government has stalled us with promises," Paul Marchal, 43, told Bild am Sonntag.
"If Prime Minister (Jean-Luc) Dehaene does not establish concrete laws his government must resign and we will form the White Party."

Marchal organised the "White March" in October, when hundreds of thousands of Belgians turned the centre of Brussels into a sea of white in protest against the failures of their political and legal sytem.
Marchal led the march with his wife Betty, the parents of three other dead girls and those of two who are still missing, all dressed in white and carrying white flowers.
He told Bild am Sonntag: "Even the agreed justice reform has up until now not led to any concrete laws. The criminals still have more rights than the victims.
"There is still no European centre for missing children. We parents do not want to wait any longer."

Since a child-sex ring was discovered in August, four girls have been found dead and two others who had been sexually abused were found in a dungeon. Police are now searching for the bodies of other missing children based on information given to them by chief suspect Marc Dutroux and others arrested with him (corrects by adding the fact that Dutroux is chief suspect).
Dehaene's Flemish and francophone Christian Democrats have been mired in accusations and scandals and public confidence in the governing system has been shattered.
Homosexual Deputy Prime Minister Elio Di Rupo was cleared last week of child sex charges and a minister in a regional government, Jean-Pierre Grafe, resigned after also being accused of paedophilia.
He said he was innocent but could not continue to function in the current over-heated climate of Belgian politics.
